title: The light in the sun (15.7–15.15)
hook: Krishna says the brightness of the sun, the moon and the fire is his
tomorrow: The two and the one beyond (15.16–15.20)

segments.voice: Yesterday, ashvattha: the world of change as an upside-down fig, cut with the axe of not clinging. Today, light.

The power goes out at night. The fridge goes quiet, the screen goes black. Someone finds a candle and strikes a match, and a small flame fills the room. Outside, the moon is lighting the street. And the whole time, without anyone noticing, a body keeps its own quiet warmth, turning the day's food into heat. Light in the sky, light in the flame, warmth inside a person: a chain of light and heat. Chapter fifteen walks down that exact chain, and at every link Krishna says the same thing: that's me.
screen: `A CANDLE IN THE DARK.` → `THE MOON OVER THE STREET.` → `WARMTH INSIDE A PERSON.`

segments.voice: It starts with you. Verse seven: a fragment of me, eternal, became the living being in the world of life. Mamaivamsha: a part of my own self. It draws the senses and the mind to itself. Verse eight gives a gentle picture: when that living self takes a body and leaves it, it carries the senses along, the way the wind carries scent from a flower. You can't see it go, but something has moved. Verse ten: the confused don't see it, staying or leaving. Those with the eye of wisdom do. Then the chain of light. Verse twelve: the brightness in the sun that lights the whole world, the light in the moon, the light in fire: know that light as mine. Verse thirteen: entering the earth, I hold up all beings with my energy; becoming the juicy moon, soma, I nourish the plants. Verse fourteen: becoming the fire of digestion in living bodies, joined with the breath going in and out, I digest the four kinds of food. So in this chapter, the divine isn't only far off. Krishna says he is the warmth in the belly after dinner. Verse fifteen brings it all the way home: I am seated in the heart of all. From me come memory, knowledge, and their loss. I am what all the Vedas are trying to know. That's why your line today is in Krishna's voice: when the Gita says I am the light, it's Krishna speaking, tracing that light from the sun to the heart.
screen: `A FRAGMENT OF ME, IN YOU.` · `LIGHT IN SUN, MOON AND FIRE.` · `THE FIRE THAT DIGESTS YOUR FOOD.` · `SEATED IN THE HEART OF ALL.` · then, large: `THE LIGHT IN THE SUN.`

segments.voice: Feel any warmth in your body, your hands, your chest, your belly; that warmth started as sunlight. Follow it back, from belly to meal, meal to field, field to sun. Then follow it home again to the center of your chest, and rest where verse fifteen says the light is seated.
Tejas, brilliance, radiance. Gita fifteen, twelve: the brightness in the sun, the moon and the fire is Krishna's light; verse fifteen says that light is seated in every heart.
Your line: I am the light. Krishna's words: sun, moon, fire, and the heart. See you at day two hundred twelve.

howItsDone: Some Hindu families and communities recite Gita chapter fifteen before meals; verse 15.14 describes the divine as the fire of digestion, which makes it a natural mealtime reading.

fork.setup: Krishna wants a picture for how the self carries the senses from one body to the next. what does he choose?
options: wind carrying scent from a flower.
fork.reveal: wind carrying scent. you can't see the scent move, but it's gone from one place and present in another.

original.note: Sanskrit: tejas, brilliance, radiance; the brightness in the sun that Krishna calls his own in Gita 15.12.

trapdoor: what you thought: 'I am the light' is a slogan.
what it means: in Gita 15 the divine says the light in sun, moon and fire, and the fire in your body, are his, and he sits in every heart.
what a scholar hears: 15.12–15.15 move from cosmic light to vaishvanara, the digestive fire joined with prana and apana, to the heart; 15.7 calls the living being 'mamaivamsha', a part of me.

notes: howItsDone says some families recite chapter 15 before meals: a known custom in some communities (e.g., parts of South India, ISKCON), but confirm phrasing.
Original word is tejas (15.12: yad aditya-gatam tejo); confirm spelling and pronunciation.
The carry 'I am the light' is framed explicitly as Krishna's words, so it doesn't read as the listener claiming divinity.
